correctness.rationale: For any two k-subsets, shortest paths must remove each element of A\B and insert each of B\A exactly once. The independent orderings give (d!)² states. Fixing adjacent ranks yields exactly four feasible midpoint states and generators (s_i,e),(e,s_i),(s_i,s_i). The edge/triangle/maximal clique formulas follow by unique moved rank. Applying a shared triangular bubble-sort comparator schedule to both orderings proves a universal binom(d,2) upper bound; reversal in one coordinate provides matching inversion lower bound. Both independent embedded programs reconstruct exact small cases, one directly from Johnson subsets and one from the generator graph. Finite checks are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparisons distinguish restricted ascending paths (Zara 2003), global rerouting complexity (Bonsma 2010), a single-copy Cayley model for hypercube geodesics (Asplund et al. 2017), and the hypercube Kendall metric (Gajjar et al. 2024). None inspected states or logically implies the paired Johnson Cayley graph, edge-disjoint K4 decomposition, or its sharp diameter. Semantic index and primary-literature searches matched only different objects. Residual priority risk is explicitly retained.

value.rationale: A uniform complete structural classification is given for shortest-path rerouting between every pair of endpoints in every Johnson graph. It exhibits a genuine structural difference from hypercube rerouting (unique K4 edge tiling for simultaneous deletion/insertion) and an exact diameter matching the one-coordinate permutohedron despite squaring the state count. The constructive common sorting network and exact clique/triangle counts make it useful for comparing rerouting models and quantifying worst-case path changes, without reliance on speculative downstream applications.
